## Varity AI Gateway

URL: https://docs.varity.so/ai-gateway/
Description: OpenAI-compatible inference on Varity. Point any OpenAI client at https://ai.varity.app/v1 and change nothing else.

The Varity AI Gateway is an OpenAI-compatible inference API. It speaks the same
chat-completions wire format as the OpenAI API, so every OpenAI SDK, framework
adapter, and agent runtime already knows how to talk to it. For chat,
streaming, tool calls, embeddings, image generation, and speech, the
integration is a one-line base-URL swap.

Two SDK calls are **not** covered by that swap, because they send
`multipart/form-data` and these routes take JSON: `images.edit` and
`audio.transcriptions` both answer `415`. Send the bytes as base64 in the JSON
body instead — the working shapes are in
[Compatibility](/ai-gateway/compatibility/#the-two-sdk-exceptions).

```text
https://ai.varity.app/v1
```

`https://ai.varity.app` is the canonical AI Gateway host. `https://varity.app/v1`
remains a compatibility alias that the edge routes to the same service, so
existing clients keep working; new integrations should use `ai.varity.app`.

Chat completions are the core, and the same host serves OpenAI-compatible
[embeddings, image generation and editing, transcription, and
speech](/ai-gateway/compatibility/) on the models whose `capabilities` advertise
them.

## Fastest Path

Set two variables and send a request. This is the whole integration.

  

    ```bash
    curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/chat/completions \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "model": "glm-5-2",
        "messages": [
          { "role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence." }
        ]
      }'
    ```

  
  

    ```python
    # pip install openai
    import os
    from openai import OpenAI

    client = OpenAI(
        base_url="https://ai.varity.app/v1",
        api_key=os.environ["VARITY_API_KEY"],
    )

    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="glm-5-2",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}],
    )

    print(response.choices[0].message.content)
    ```

  
  

    ```javascript
    // npm install openai
    import OpenAI from "openai";

    const client = new OpenAI({
      baseURL: "https://ai.varity.app/v1",
      apiKey: process.env.VARITY_API_KEY,
    });

    const response = await client.chat.completions.create({
      model: "glm-5-2",
      messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Say hello in one sentence." }],
    });

    console.log(response.choices[0].message.content);
    ```

  

`base_url` / `baseURL` is the only line that differs from an OpenAI setup. Model
ids come from the Varity catalog, not OpenAI's. See
[Models](/ai-gateway/models/) for the full list.

## Confirm The Gateway Before You Have A Key

`GET /v1/models` is public. Run it right now, with no credential, and you get a
`200` plus the live catalog:

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/models
```

```json
{
  "object": "list",
  "privacy_scope": "anonymized",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "glm-5-2",
      "display_name": "GLM 5.2",
      "object": "model",
      "owned_by": "varity",
      "maker": { "key": "zai", "label": "Z.ai" },
      "capabilities": {
        "input_modalities": ["text", "document"],
        "output_modalities": ["text"],
        "chat_completions": true,
        "tool_calls": true,
        "streaming": true,
        "streaming_tool_calls": true
      },
      "context_window": 1000000,
      "max_completion_tokens": 131072,
      "privacy": "private",
      "privacy_routes": ["private"],
      "availability": { "status": "available" },
      "customer_pricing": {
        "status": "configured",
        "currency": "usd",
        "unit": "per_million_tokens",
        "input": "<live rate>",
        "output": "<live rate>",
        "cached_input": "<live rate>"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The entry above is trimmed, and the rates are placeholders: `input`, `output`,
and `cached_input` are numbers in the real response. Read prices from
`GET /v1/models` or the **Models** tab on the portal's AI Gateway page, never
from this page.

The gateway also exposes unauthenticated health and readiness probes on the
canonical host:

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/healthz
curl https://ai.varity.app/readyz
```

```text
{ "status": "ok", "service": "varity-ai-gateway", "version": "<deployed build>", "source_commit": "<commit>" }
```

`/readyz` adds `servable` and `published` model counts. The `version` field
reports the deployed gateway build; re-probe for the current one rather than
pinning it in your own config.

## Authentication

Inference requests require a Varity API key sent as a bearer credential:

```text
Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY
```

Create keys on the Developer Portal's [AI Gateway page](https://developer.store.varity.so/dashboard/ai-gateway?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=docs-to-portal&utm_content=ai-gateway-api-keys), under the
**Inference keys** tab, or with `POST /v1/keys` from a signed-in portal session.
Key plaintext is shown once
at creation and is never returned again; the list identifies each key by its
key id (`vki_…`). The same key format is used across the
Varity [public API](/ai-tools/api-reference/). A revoked key stops working
within 30 seconds. See [Billing and Keys](/ai-gateway/billing-and-keys/).

Inference is prepaid: add credits on the **Gateway billing** tab before your
first request. Each request is charged its provider cost, and Varity's 5%
service fee is charged when credits are added.

Auth is enforced on every inference route. A request with no `Authorization`
header returns `401`:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "A bearer credential is required.",
    "type": "authentication_error",
    "code": "authentication_required",
    "param": null,
    "retryable": false,
    "request_id": "516c24ef-ba5a-4e3d-8f32-0a609ae5d298"
  }
}
```

A malformed, revoked, or expired key also returns `401` with
`code: "authentication_required"`; only the message differs:
`The provided credential is invalid or expired.` Treat any `401` as "send a
valid key" rather than branching on the message text.

Authentication is checked before the request body is validated. An unauthenticated
request naming a nonexistent model still returns the authentication error, not a
model error.

## Streaming

Set `stream: true` for server-sent events, exactly as with OpenAI. Read
`capabilities.streaming` per model rather than assuming it is universal.

  

    ```bash
    curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/chat/completions \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "model": "glm-5-2",
        "stream": true,
        "messages": [
          { "role": "user", "content": "Count to five." }
        ]
      }'
    ```

  
  

    ```python
    stream = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="glm-5-2",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Count to five."}],
        stream=True,
    )

    for chunk in stream:
        delta = chunk.choices[0].delta.content
        if delta:
            print(delta, end="")
    ```

  
  

    ```javascript
    const stream = await client.chat.completions.create({
      model: "glm-5-2",
      messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Count to five." }],
      stream: true,
    });

    for await (const chunk of stream) {
      process.stdout.write(chunk.choices[0]?.delta?.content ?? "");
    }
    ```

  

Streaming *tool calls* are a narrower capability than streaming text, and are
only supported on some models. Check `capabilities.streaming_tool_calls` before
you combine `stream: true` with `tools`. See
[Compatibility](/ai-gateway/compatibility/).

## Errors

Errors use the OpenAI error envelope, with two Varity additions: `retryable` and
`request_id`.

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `error.message` | Human-readable description |
| `error.type` | Error class, for example `authentication_error` |
| `error.code` | Stable machine code, for example `authentication_required` |
| `error.param` | Offending request field, or `null` |
| `error.retryable` | Whether retrying the same request can succeed |
| `error.request_id` | Correlation id, also returned as the `x-request-id` response header |

Quote `request_id` in any support request. It is present on both the response
body and the `x-request-id` header on every response, including successful ones.
The gateway generates it; a caller-supplied `x-request-id` header is not echoed.

## Rate Limits

Inference is bounded two ways at once: **120 requests per minute** and **4
concurrent requests**, both counted across your whole account rather than per
key. Crossing either returns `429`, before any model provider is called.

Read your own numbers instead of hardcoding these defaults:

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/inference/policy \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "object": "inference.tenant_policy",
  "privacy_floor": "anonymized",
  "requests_per_minute": 120,
  "concurrency_limit": 4,
  "limits_scope": "account"
}
```

`GET /v1/models` is public and carries no request budget at all. The budgets,
the exact headers each refusal returns, and the body-size ceilings are on
[AI Gateway Rate Limits](/ai-gateway/limits/).

## AI Gateway Billing and Keys

URL: https://docs.varity.so/ai-gateway/billing-and-keys/
Description: How Varity AI Gateway credits, the 5% service fee, top-ups, inference keys, and usage reporting work.

The AI Gateway is prepaid. You add credits, each request is charged from that
balance, and an inference key is what your code sends to spend it.

## How You Are Charged

- **Each request is charged exactly its provider cost.** No markup is added per
  request.
- **Varity's 5% service fee is charged when you add credits**, on top of the
  amount you add. A $20.00 top-up charges your card $21.00 and adds $20.00 of
  credits.
- **A top-up is between $20 and $1,000.**
- **A payment method is required.** There is no automatic sign-up credit, and you
  cannot bring your own provider key.

These terms are machine-readable in the `x-varity-commercial-contract` block of
`GET https://ai.varity.app/v1/openapi.json`:

```json
{
  "managed_rate": "actual_provider_cost",
  "funding_service_fee_percent": 5,
  "minimum_refill_usd": 20,
  "maximum_refill_usd": 1000,
  "payment_method_required": true,
  "automatic_signup_credit": false,
  "byok": "unavailable"
}
```

Per-model rates are in `customer_pricing` on
[`GET /v1/models`](/ai-gateway/models/#pricing) and on the **Models** tab of the
portal's AI Gateway page. This page lists no prices, because the catalog changes
without a docs release.

When the balance cannot cover a request, or your monthly spending limit is
reached, the request is refused with `402 insufficient_gateway_balance` before
any model is called.

## Adding Credits

Add credits on the **Gateway billing** tab of the AI Gateway page in the
Developer Portal. The same tab sets a monthly spending limit and auto-reload.

Auto-reload tops the balance up when it falls below a threshold. Its amount
follows the same $20 to $1,000 bounds and the same 5% fee, and the threshold
must be lower than the amount.

## Inference Keys

Create, list, and revoke keys on the **Inference keys** tab.

- The key plaintext is shown **once**, when the key is created. Store it then;
  it is never returned again.
- Each key is identified by an id of the form `vki_…`.
- A key can be limited to a list of up to 64 model ids. An empty list allows
  every model, including models added later.
- A key has a privacy floor, `private` or `anonymized`. An `anonymized` key
  requires the account itself to allow anonymized processing first.
- A key can carry its own `requests_per_minute` and `concurrency_limit` (the
  smaller of the key's and the account's bound applies), a spending budget, and
  an expiry.
- **A revoked key stops working within 30 seconds.**

Send the key as a bearer credential on every inference request:

```text
Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY
```

## Account Routes

The portal tabs are built on these routes on `https://ai.varity.app`. They take
a **Developer Portal session** as the bearer credential. An inference key is
refused on them with `403 portal_session_required`, so a leaked inference key
cannot mint more keys, move money, or change privacy settings.

| Route | What it does |
|-------|--------------|
| `POST /v1/keys` | Creates an inference key. Body: `name` (1 to 80 characters), `allowed_models` (array, may be empty), `privacy_floor`, and optionally `requests_per_minute`, `concurrency_limit`, `upstream_budget_usd`, `expires_at` (Unix seconds), `project_id`, `application_id`, `environment`. |
| `GET /v1/keys` | Lists the account's inference keys. No plaintext is ever returned. |
| `GET /v1/keys/audit` | Key lifecycle events. Accepts `limit` from 1 to 500. |
| `POST /v1/keys/{id}/revoke` | Revokes one of the account's own keys. |
| `GET /v1/billing/balance` | The balance: `availableBalanceUsd`, `reservedUsd`, `spendThisMonthUsd`, `monthlySpendingLimitUsd`, `autoReload`, and more. |
| `GET /v1/billing/transactions` | Balance transactions. Accepts `limit` from 1 to 100 (default 50) and `offset` from 0 to 10,000. |
| `PATCH /v1/billing/settings` | Sets `monthlySpendingLimitCents` (`null`, or 100 to 10,000,000) and `autoReload` `{ enabled, thresholdCents, amountCents }`. |
| `POST /v1/billing/top-up` | Starts a card checkout. Body: `email` (must belong to your account) and `balanceCents` (2,000 to 100,000). Returns the checkout `url` plus `balanceCents`, `serviceFeeCents`, and `totalCents`. |
| `PUT /v1/inference/policy` | Sets the account privacy floor. See [Privacy Routing](/ai-gateway/compatibility/#privacy-routing). |

The request budgets for these routes are on
[Rate Limits](/ai-gateway/limits/#account-routes).

## Usage And Request History

These routes accept an **inference key**, so your own code can read what it has
spent:

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/inference/usage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY"
```

| Route | What it returns |
|-------|-----------------|
| `GET /v1/inference/usage` | Requests, tokens, and `spend_usd` for the current period, with breakdowns. |
| `GET /v1/inference/requests` | Per-request metadata. Filters: `limit` (1 to 100), `cursor`, `model`, `state`, `created_after`, `created_before`. |
| `GET /v1/inference/performance` | Latency percentiles. `window` is `1h`, `24h`, `7d`, or `30d`. |
| `GET /v1/inference/policy` | Your privacy floor and rate limits. |

Request records hold metadata only, never prompt or response content, and are
kept for 30 days. See
[Privacy And Data Retention](/ai-gateway/compatibility/#privacy-and-data-retention).

## Next Steps

- **[Endpoints](/ai-gateway/endpoints/)**: a minimal request for every inference route
- **[Rate Limits](/ai-gateway/limits/)**: request budgets and the `429` bodies
- **[Models](/ai-gateway/models/)**: per-model pricing fields

## AI Gateway OpenAI Compatibility

URL: https://docs.varity.so/ai-gateway/compatibility/
Description: Exactly which parts of the OpenAI API surface the Varity AI Gateway implements, and which parts it does not.

"OpenAI-compatible" is a claim about a surface, not a promise about all of it.
This page states the boundary. An exclusion you discover at runtime instead of
reading it here is a documentation bug. If you hit one, report it.

Everything below was checked against the live gateway at
`https://ai.varity.app/v1`, its canonical host, and against the contract it
publishes at `GET /v1/openapi.json`. `https://varity.app/v1` is a compatibility
alias routed to the same service and serves the same surface.

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Status |
|----------|--------|
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | **Supported.** Requires a bearer API key. Streaming and tool-call generation on eligible models. |
| `GET /v1/models` | **Supported.** Public, no key required. |
| `POST /v1/embeddings` | **Supported.** Requires a bearer API key. Only a model whose `capabilities.output_modalities` includes `embedding` is routable. |
| `POST /v1/images/generations` | **Supported.** Requires a bearer API key. Image-capable models only; results are returned inline as base64 and never stored. |
| `POST /v1/images/edits` | **Supported.** Requires a bearer API key. JSON with base64 image data (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/webp`); a source image or mask at or above 25 MB is rejected. |
| `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` | **Supported.** Requires a bearer API key. JSON with the audio as a base64 typed part; the model must advertise `capabilities.transcription`. Returns JSON, or plain text when `response_format` is `text`. No streaming mode. |
| `POST /v1/audio/speech` | **Supported.** Requires a bearer API key. The model must advertise `capabilities.speech` and the format must be one of its `capabilities.speech_formats`. Returns audio bytes with a matching `audio/*` content type; `stream: true` gives a chunked binary response, not SSE. |
| `GET /v1/models/{id}` | **Not implemented.** Returns `404`. Fetch the list and filter client-side. |
| `POST /v1/completions` (legacy text completions) | **Not implemented.** Returns `404`. |
| `POST /v1/responses` | **Not implemented.** Returns `404`. |
| `/v1/assistants` | **Not implemented.** Returns `404`. |
| `/v1/files` | **Not implemented.** Returns `404`. |
| `/v1/vector_stores` | **Not implemented.** Returns `404`. |
| `POST /v1/moderations` | **Not implemented.** Returns `404`. |
| `/v1/batches` | **Not implemented.** Returns `404`. |
| `/v1/fine_tuning/jobs` | **Not implemented.** Returns `404`. |

Beyond the OpenAI surface, the gateway serves its own endpoints. These have no
OpenAI equivalent, so a client written against the OpenAI spec will not find
them, but they are public and stable.

| Endpoint | Status |
|----------|--------|
| `GET /v1/openapi.json` | **Supported.** Public, no key required. The machine-readable contract for this surface, including the data-handling block below. |
| `GET /v1/inference/requests` | **Supported.** Requires a bearer API key. Per-request metadata. `created_after` and `created_before` take RFC 3339 timestamps; send them with fractional seconds, for example `2026-09-16T00:00:00.000Z`. |
| `GET /v1/inference/usage` | **Supported.** Requires a bearer API key. |
| `GET /v1/inference/policy` | **Supported.** Requires a bearer API key. Returns the privacy floor (`private` or `anonymized`) enforced for the account, and the account's `requests_per_minute`, `concurrency_limit` and `limits_scope`; with a scoped key the key's effective floor and its own limit overrides are reported beside them. |
| `GET /v1/inference/performance` | **Supported.** Requires a bearer API key. Accepts `window` of `1h`, `24h`, `7d`, or `30d`. |

### Account routes

The AI Gateway host also serves the account routes for its own keys, prepaid
balance, and privacy entitlement. These require a Developer Portal session token
as the bearer credential; an inference API key is refused on them.

| Endpoint | Status |
|----------|--------|
| `GET /v1/keys` | **Supported.** Secret-free list of the account's inference keys. |
| `POST /v1/keys` | **Supported.** Mints an inference-only key; the plaintext is returned exactly once. |
| `GET /v1/keys/audit` | **Supported.** Secret-free key lifecycle events. Accepts `limit`. |
| `POST /v1/keys/{id}/revoke` | **Supported.** Revokes one of the account's own keys. |
| `PUT /v1/inference/policy` | **Supported.** Sets the account's privacy floor to `private` or `anonymized`. `anonymized` is the default for an account that never chose; choosing `anonymized` requires `acknowledge_anonymized_processing: true`. |
| `GET /v1/billing/balance` | **Supported.** The prepaid Gateway balance. |
| `GET /v1/billing/transactions` | **Supported.** Balance transactions. Accepts `limit` and `offset`. |
| `PATCH /v1/billing/settings` | **Supported.** Monthly spending limit and auto-reload. |
| `POST /v1/billing/top-up` | **Supported.** Starts a card checkout that funds the balance: $20 minimum, $1,000 maximum, plus Varity's 5% service fee. See [Billing and Keys](/ai-gateway/billing-and-keys/). |

The same keys can also be created from the platform API with
`POST /api/api-keys/inference`; see the
[Public API Reference](/ai-tools/api-reference/).

Hosted tool execution, batch, files, assistants, fine-tuning, and moderation
are not part of the surface. Unimplemented routes return `404` with the JSON
error envelope below (`code: "invalid_request"`, message `Route not found.`).
Branch on the HTTP status code, not on the message text.

Unauthenticated health and readiness probes are available outside `/v1` on the
canonical host:

| Endpoint | Status |
|----------|--------|
| `GET /healthz` | **Supported.** Public. Returns `{"status":"ok","service":"varity-ai-gateway","version":"<deployed build>","source_commit":"<commit>"}` (re-probe for the current build rather than pinning it). |
| `GET /readyz` | **Supported.** Public. Same fields plus `servable`, `published`, and `minimum_servable` model counts. |

Any OpenAI SDK helper that touches an unimplemented route will fail, including
the Assistants and Responses APIs, file upload helpers, and batch. The
`chat.completions`, `models`, `embeddings`, `images.generate`, and
`audio.speech` namespaces work unchanged, on the models whose `capabilities`
advertise them. `images.edit` and `audio.transcriptions` need a different call
shape — see below.

## The Two SDK Exceptions

"Point your OpenAI client at the base URL and change nothing else" is true for
every route except two. `images.edit` and `audio.transcriptions` are the
operations the OpenAI SDKs send as `multipart/form-data`, and these routes
accept `application/json` only. A multipart request is refused with `415`:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "This endpoint accepts application/json only: send the audio as audio.data (base64) with audio.media_type. multipart/form-data is not accepted.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "invalid_request",
    "param": null,
    "retryable": false,
    "request_id": "…"
  }
}
```

The refusal names the JSON shape rather than blaming a field you did send. Call
these two with a plain HTTP client and inline base64:

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/images/edits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "<an image-capable model id>",
    "prompt": "Make the sky orange.",
    "image": { "data": "<base64 bytes>", "mime_type": "image/png" }
  }'
```

`image.mime_type` is one of `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, or `image/webp`. An
optional `mask` takes the same `{ data, mime_type }` shape, and `size` is
optional.

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "<a transcription model id>",
    "audio": { "data": "<base64 bytes>", "media_type": "audio/mpeg" }
  }'
```

`audio.media_type` is one of `audio/wav`, `audio/wave`, `audio/x-wav`,
`audio/flac`, `audio/x-flac`, `audio/mp4`, `audio/m4a`, `audio/x-m4a`,
`audio/aac`, `audio/mpeg`, `audio/ogg`, `audio/oga`, or `audio/webm`. Optional
fields are `audio.filename`, `response_format` (`json` or `text`), `language`,
and `timestamps`. Decoded audio must be under 25 MB.

Both shapes are on `GET /v1/openapi.json`, so you can generate a client from
the contract rather than transcribing this page.

## Per-Model Capabilities

Compatibility is not uniform across models. Each catalog entry carries a
`capabilities` object, and you must read it. The same request that works
against one model can be unsupported on another.

| Capability | Models supporting it |
|------------|----------------------|
| `chat_completions` | The chat models; image, audio, and embedding models report `false` |
| `streaming` | Most, but not all, chat models |
| `tool_calls` | A subset of the chat models |
| `streaming_tool_calls` | A smaller subset; absent on a few entries, which means unproven, not unsupported |
| `output_modalities` | `text`, `embedding`, `image`, or `audio`: the route a model belongs on |
| `transcription`, `speech` | The audio models, each on exactly one of the two audio routes |

### Tool calling is the exception, not the default

Only a subset of the catalog accepts `tools` / `tool_choice`. If your agent
framework assumes function calling works everywhere, as most do, it will break on
the models that report `tool_calls: false`. Resolve this at runtime rather than
hardcoding a list:

```python
models = {m["id"]: m for m in client.models.list().model_dump()["data"]}

def supports_tools(model_id, streaming=False):
    caps = models[model_id]["capabilities"]
    return caps["streaming_tool_calls"] if streaming else caps["tool_calls"]
```

The OpenAI Python SDK exposes only the fields it knows about on typed objects.
Varity's extra fields (`capabilities`, `context_window`, `customer_pricing`)
arrive as extra JSON, so read the raw dict (or call `/v1/models` directly with an
HTTP client) rather than expecting SDK attributes for them.

## Model Identifiers

Varity model ids are **not** guaranteed to be OpenAI model ids. Some entries now
carry OpenAI-style names such as `gpt-4o`, but every id is a Varity catalog entry
with Varity routing and pricing, and there is no aliasing layer that maps an
OpenAI name onto a different model. A request naming an id that is not in the
live catalog is a request for a model that does not exist here.

Ids are readable human slugs, for example `glm-5-1`, `glm-5-2`,
`llama-3-3-70b`, and `qwen-3-5-35b-a3b`. Always take ids from
[the live catalog](/ai-gateway/models/).

## Limits That Differ From OpenAI

- **`max_completion_tokens` is per-model and often small.** The ceiling is independent of the context window, so a very large context does not mean a long reply is allowed. Read both fields per model.
- **Cached-input pricing is per model.** Some models price `cached_input` below `input` and others price them the same. Read `customer_pricing.cached_input` per model.
- **There is a concurrency bound as well as a rate limit.** Inference is held to 120 requests per minute *and* 4 in-flight requests, both counted for the whole account rather than per key. `GET /v1/inference/policy` publishes your own numbers. See [Rate Limits](/ai-gateway/limits/).
- **`GET /v1/models` carries no request budget** and returns no `RateLimit-*` headers. The headers live on the inference and inference-read routes, not on catalog discovery.

## Errors

The error envelope matches OpenAI's shape and adds two fields:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "The provided credential is invalid or expired.",
    "type": "authentication_error",
    "code": "authentication_required",
    "param": null,
    "retryable": false,
    "request_id": "504f4a24-1427-4483-89fe-ad332fdad5d6"
  }
}
```

- `retryable` is a boolean OpenAI does not send. Use it instead of guessing from the status code whether to retry.
- `request_id` is also returned as the `x-request-id` response header on every response, successful or not. The gateway generates it; a caller-supplied `x-request-id` header is not echoed.

A managed-inference failure adds a diagnostic block naming who decided the
failure and where in the request's life it happened:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `diagnostic_code` | `ai_gateway.<code>`. |
| `failure_cause` | The same value as `code`. |
| `failure_domain` | `varity_projection` (Varity refused), `supplier_observed` (a model provider answered and Varity observed it), or `dependency_observed` (a Varity-operated dependency was unreachable, named in `dependency`). |
| `lifecycle_stage` | `admission`, `provider_attempt`, `settlement`, or `terminal`. |
| `action` | What to do next, in one sentence. |

### Error Codes

Branch on `code`. `error.retryable` is on every body and is authoritative for
that response; the column below is what the gateway publishes today.

**Varity refused the request** (`failure_domain: "varity_projection"`):

| Code | HTTP | Retryable | Cause |
|------|------|-----------|-------|
| `authentication_required` | `401` | no | No bearer credential, or one that is invalid, revoked, or expired. |
| `invalid_request` | `400` | no | The body failed validation. Also `404` on an unimplemented route, `413` when the body exceeds the route ceiling, and `415` on `multipart/form-data`. |
| `input_modality_unsupported` | `400` | no | Every route for this model rejected the supplied image or document part. Distinct from `invalid_request` so you can tell "this model cannot see" from "this body is malformed". |
| `model_not_found` | `404` | no | The id is not in the live catalog. |
| `model_not_allowed` | `403` | no | The model exists but this credential's model scope excludes it. |
| `tenant_not_admitted` | `403` | no | Managed inference is not enabled for the account, or the key is expired. |
| `privacy_policy_violation` | `403` | no | The request asked for a privacy floor weaker than the account's. |
| `duplicate_request` | `409` | no | The idempotency identity was already admitted. |
| `request_cancelled` | `408` | no | The deadline elapsed, or the caller closed the socket. |
| `rate_limit_exceeded` | `429` | yes | The account's requests-per-minute budget is exhausted. See [Rate Limits](/ai-gateway/limits/). |
| `concurrency_limit_exceeded` | `429` | yes | The account's in-flight bound is exhausted. |
| `budget_exceeded` | `429` | yes | The account's inference budget for the period is exhausted. |
| `payment_method_required` | `402` | no | No active payment method. |
| `insufficient_gateway_balance` | `402` | no | The prepaid AI Gateway balance cannot cover the request. |
| `gateway_balance_frozen` | `402` | no | The balance is frozen pending billing review. |
| `billing_unavailable` | `503` | yes | The isolated billing ledger could not answer. Not your request's fault. |
| `internal_error` | `500` | no | An unclassified gateway failure. Quote `request_id`. |

**A model provider decided it** (`failure_domain: "supplier_observed"`):

| Code | HTTP | Retryable | Cause |
|------|------|-----------|-------|
| `model_unavailable` | `503` | yes | No callable route for this model right now. Choose another model or retry. |
| `privacy_route_unavailable` | `403` | no | The model has no callable route at the required privacy level. |
| `upstream_rate_limited` | `429` | yes | The provider is rate-limiting. Carries `Retry-After` only when the provider published its own reset. |
| `upstream_unavailable` | `503` | yes | No qualified route answered. |
| `upstream_balance_exhausted` | varies | no | Provider funding is exhausted. Varity's problem, not yours; pick another model. |
| `upstream_timeout` | varies | yes | The provider did not answer in time. Retry only if the request is known not to have taken effect. |
| `stream_terminated` | — | no | A stream ended mid-flight. Do not replay an ambiguously chargeable stream; inspect the correlated request instead. |

`upstream_authentication_failed` exists in the gateway's internal vocabulary but
never reaches you. A refused Varity provider credential is something only Varity
can fix, so it is published as `model_unavailable` — the one thing a caller can
act on — and the real cause stays in the operator record.

Authentication is evaluated **before** request-body validation, so an
unauthenticated request with an invalid `model` returns the authentication
error, not a model error. Do not use the error type to infer that your payload
was accepted.

These codes are the AI Gateway's own. The platform API at `varity.app/api` uses
a **different envelope and a different code vocabulary** — see
[API Errors](/api/errors/). In particular the AI Gateway never emits
`invalid_api_key`; an invalid key here is `authentication_required`.

## Privacy And Data Retention

The gateway publishes its data-handling contract as an `x-varity-data-handling`
block at the root of `GET /v1/openapi.json`. It is machine-readable, so you can
assert against it in CI rather than taking a page's word for it.

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| `inference_metadata_retention_days` | `30` |
| `stored_content` | `[]` |
| `content_never_stored` | `prompts`, `responses`, `tool_arguments`, `uploaded_content`, `generated_image_bytes`, `playground_conversations` |
| `generated_image_retention` | `inline_only` |
| `financial_and_security_records` | `separate_retention_classes` |

Prompt, response, uploaded, and generated-image bytes are never written to the
inference records. What is retained for 30 days is request metadata: model id,
token counts, latency, fallback count, error code, and timestamps. Read it back
with `GET /v1/inference/requests`.

This is the property usually searched for as zero data retention, or ZDR.

## Privacy Routing

The live catalog reports two routing privacy classes: `privacy: "private"` with
`privacy_routes: ["private"]`, and `privacy: "anonymized"` with
`privacy_routes: ["anonymized"]`. This field has no OpenAI equivalent; it is
Varity-specific catalog metadata describing how each model is routed. Read it per
model.

Your account has a privacy floor. It is `anonymized` unless you choose
otherwise, which lets requests use both `private` and `anonymized` models. Set it
to `private` with `PUT /v1/inference/policy` (or on the portal's **Gateway
settings** tab) and only `private` models are callable. A single chat request can
tighten the floor, never loosen it, with
`"varity_extensions": { "privacy_floor": "private" }`; asking for a weaker floor
than the account's returns `403 privacy_policy_violation`.

## AI Gateway Endpoints

URL: https://docs.varity.so/ai-gateway/endpoints/
Description: One minimal request for every Varity AI Gateway route, with the full schema at /v1/openapi.json.

Every route is served from `https://ai.varity.app`. The full machine-readable
schema is public, needs no key, and is the source for anything this page leaves
out:

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/openapi.json
```

Replace `<… model id>` in the examples with an `id` from
[`GET /v1/models`](/ai-gateway/models/) whose `capabilities` fit the route. For
example, `output_modalities` containing `embedding` for embeddings, `image` for
images, `capabilities.speech` for speech, and `capabilities.transcription` for
transcription.

## Discovery

### `GET /v1/models`

The live catalog. Public, no key.

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/models
```

### `GET /v1/openapi.json`

The contract for this surface, including its commercial and data-handling
terms. Public, no key.

## Inference

All inference routes take an inference key as `Authorization: Bearer …` and a
JSON body. Each request may run for at most 120 seconds.

### `POST /v1/chat/completions`

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "glm-5-2",
    "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence." }]
  }'
```

Required: `model`, `messages`. Optional fields include `stream`,
`max_completion_tokens`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `stop`, `seed`,
`response_format`, `reasoning_effort`, `tools`, `tool_choice`, and
`parallel_tool_calls`. Each works only on models whose `capabilities` advertise
it.

A message's `content` can be an array of parts: `text`, `image_url` (an https URL
or a base64 `data:` URL), and `document` (`{ "url": …, "filename": … }`), on
models whose `capabilities.input_modalities` include `image` or `document`.

Varity-specific options go in `varity_extensions`:

| Field | Effect |
|-------|--------|
| `web_search` | Ground the answer in a live web search, on models with `capabilities.web_search`. |
| `web_scraping` | Read up to 5 pages linked from the latest user message. |
| `privacy_floor` | Tighten, never loosen, the account privacy floor for this request. |

Two optional headers:

| Header | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| `Idempotency-Key` | Send the same key when retrying. Reuse returns `409 duplicate_request` instead of charging twice. |
| `X-Varity-Deadline-Ms` | Absolute Unix-epoch deadline in milliseconds, capped at 120 seconds from receipt. |

Streaming is covered on the [overview](/ai-gateway/#streaming).

### `POST /v1/embeddings`

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "model": "<embedding model id>", "input": "The quick brown fox." }'
```

`input` is a string or an array of up to 2,048 strings. Optional:
`encoding_format` (`float` or `base64`) and `dimensions`.

### `POST /v1/images/generations`

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/images/generations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "model": "<image model id>", "prompt": "A red cube on a table" }'
```

Optional: `size` and `n`. Images come back inline as base64 in
`data[].b64_json` with a `mime_type`, and Varity never stores them.

### `POST /v1/images/edits`

JSON with the image as base64, not `multipart/form-data`:

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/images/edits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "<image model id>",
    "prompt": "Make the sky orange.",
    "image": { "data": "<base64 bytes>", "mime_type": "image/png" }
  }'
```

See [The Two SDK Exceptions](/ai-gateway/compatibility/#the-two-sdk-exceptions).

### `POST /v1/audio/speech`

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/audio/speech \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "model": "<speech model id>", "input": "Hello from Varity.", "response_format": "mp3" }' \
  --output hello.mp3
```

`response_format` must be one of the model's `capabilities.speech_formats`.
Optional: `voice`, `speed`, `language`, `prompt`, and `stream`. The response is
audio bytes, not JSON.

### `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions`

JSON with the audio as base64, not `multipart/form-data`:

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "<transcription model id>",
    "audio": { "data": "<base64 bytes>", "media_type": "audio/mpeg" }
  }'
```

Optional: `response_format` (`json` or `text`), `language`, and `timestamps`.

## Your Account, With An Inference Key

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/inference/policy \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY"
```

| Route | Returns |
|-------|---------|
| `GET /v1/inference/policy` | Privacy floor and rate limits |
| `GET /v1/inference/usage` | Requests, tokens, and spend for the period |
| `GET /v1/inference/requests` | Per-request metadata |
| `GET /v1/inference/performance` | Latency percentiles for a `window` |

## Your Account, With A Portal Session

Keys, billing, and the privacy setting are managed from the Developer Portal.
These routes refuse an inference key:

`POST /v1/keys`, `GET /v1/keys`, `GET /v1/keys/audit`,
`POST /v1/keys/{id}/revoke`, `PUT /v1/inference/policy`,
`GET /v1/billing/balance`, `GET /v1/billing/transactions`,
`PATCH /v1/billing/settings`, `POST /v1/billing/top-up`.

Each is described on [Billing and Keys](/ai-gateway/billing-and-keys/#account-routes).

## Health

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/healthz
curl https://ai.varity.app/readyz
```

Public, no key, outside `/v1`.

`https://varity.app/v1` is an alias for the same service. Use
`https://ai.varity.app/v1` in new code.

## AI Gateway Rate Limits

URL: https://docs.varity.so/ai-gateway/limits/
Description: The request budgets, concurrency bound, and body-size ceilings the Varity AI Gateway enforces, the headers it actually returns, and what each 429 body looks like.

The AI Gateway (`https://ai.varity.app/v1`) is a separate surface from the
Varity platform API and enforces its own budgets. Nothing on
[Rate Limits](/api/limits/) applies here, and nothing here applies there.

Two different mechanisms are at work, and they return different headers. Read
the one that covers the route you are calling.

| Routes | Bound | Where it comes from |
|--------|-------|---------------------|
| Inference (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/images/*`, `/v1/audio/*`) | 120 requests per minute **and** 4 concurrent requests | Admission, per account |
| Inference reads (`/v1/inference/policy`, `/requests`, `/usage`, `/performance`) | 120 requests per 60-second window | A request budget, per account |
| `GET /v1/models`, `GET /v1/openapi.json` | No credential and no request budget | Public discovery |
| Account routes (`/v1/keys*`, `/v1/billing/*`, `PUT /v1/inference/policy`) | See [Account routes](#account-routes) | A request budget, per account |

## Read Your Own Limits

Do not hardcode the defaults. `GET /v1/inference/policy` publishes the numbers
your account is actually held to:

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/inference/policy \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VARITY_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "object": "inference.tenant_policy",
  "privacy_floor": "anonymized",
  "requests_per_minute": 120,
  "concurrency_limit": 4,
  "limits_scope": "account"
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `requests_per_minute` | Inference requests admitted per fixed 60-second window. |
| `concurrency_limit` | Inference requests that may be in flight at once. |
| `limits_scope` | Always `account`. Both bounds are counted globally for the account. |
| `credential_requests_per_minute` | Present only when you authenticate with a scoped key that carries its own lower rpm bound; `null` when it does not. |
| `credential_concurrency_limit` | The same, for concurrency. |

`requests_per_minute`, `concurrency_limit`, and `limits_scope` are absent when
the account has no admission policy yet. Absent means "no bound to state", not
"unlimited" — treat it as unknown and pace conservatively.

`limits_scope: "account"` means the budget is shared. Every API key your account
owns draws from the same 120 requests per minute and the same 4 concurrent
slots, and so does the Developer Portal Playground. The gateway runs on more
than one replica, and the bounds are counted across all of them — **do not
multiply a limit by the number of replicas you think are running.**

A key can carry its own `requests_per_minute` or `concurrency_limit`. When it
does, the account bound is checked first and the key's bound second, so the key
is held to **the smaller of the two**. Neither number alone is the whole truth,
which is why the policy route reports them side by side rather than merging
them.

## Inference: 120 Per Minute And 4 In Flight

The default self-service policy is 120 requests per minute over a fixed
60-second interval, and 4 concurrent in-flight requests. A request that crosses
either bound is refused at admission, before any model provider is called, so a
refused request costs nothing.

### Which Bound You Will Actually Meet

In practice, **the concurrency bound is the one that stops you**, and most
callers will never see the per-minute refusal at all.

The arithmetic is simple. With 4 slots, reaching 120 requests per minute means
sustaining 2 requests per second, which means every response must come back in
under 2 seconds. Real chat completions rarely do.

Measured on 2026-09-17 against gateway `0.3.66`, on the cheapest chat model
with `max_tokens: 1` — about as fast as a real request gets:

| Client concurrency | Requests sent | Result | Elapsed | Effective rate |
|--------------------|---------------|--------|---------|----------------|
| 3 | 130 | 130 × `200`, zero `429` | 140.0 s | ≈ 56 / min |
| 4 | 150 | 150 × `200`, zero `429` | 126.9 s | ≈ 71 / min |

Each request took roughly 3.2 to 3.4 seconds end to end, so 4 slots cap
throughput near 70 per minute — comfortably under the 120 bound, which is why
neither run produced a single `rate_limit_exceeded`.

The practical consequences:

- **Size your worker pool to the concurrency limit, not the per-minute one.** A
  pool of 4 is the account's real ceiling. Widening it past 4 buys no
  throughput and converts the surplus workers into `429`s.
- You can still reach the per-minute bound with unusually fast responses, or by
  spreading work across many keys — but both bounds are **account-scoped**, so
  extra keys on the same account share the same budget and buy nothing.
- Read both numbers from `GET /v1/inference/policy` rather than assuming the
  defaults; an account may be provisioned differently.

### The Two Refusals

Both are `429`, and both pace you — but not with the same header set, because
they are not the same kind of bound:

| Header | `rate_limit_exceeded` | `concurrency_limit_exceeded` | `upstream_rate_limited` |
|--------|----------------------|------------------------------|--------------------------|
| `Retry-After` | yes — the window (`60`) | yes — the nearest in-flight deadline | only if the provider published its own reset |
| `RateLimit-Limit` | yes | yes | no |
| `RateLimit-Remaining` | `0` | `0` | no |
| `RateLimit-Reset` | yes — same value as `Retry-After` | yes — same value as `Retry-After` | no |
| `RateLimit-Policy` | yes — `120;w=60` | **no** — the bound has no window | no |

Each bound also exists at two scopes. The account's bound is reported with the
message `The tenant request rate limit is exhausted.` /
`The tenant concurrency limit is exhausted.`; a key carrying its own lower
override reports `The API key …` instead. The `code` is identical either way,
so branch on `code` and read `GET /v1/inference/policy` to see which bound
applies to you.

### `rate_limit_exceeded`

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "The tenant request rate limit is exhausted.",
    "type": "rate_limit_error",
    "code": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "param": null,
    "request_id": "…",
    "diagnostic_code": "ai_gateway.rate_limit_exceeded",
    "failure_cause": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "failure_domain": "varity_projection",
    "lifecycle_stage": "admission",
    "action": "Retry after the credential rate-limit window resets.",
    "retryable": true
  }
}
```

Status `429`. It carries the full set of pacing headers, including the policy,
because this bound *is* counted over a window:

```text
retry-after: 60
ratelimit-limit: 120
ratelimit-remaining: 0
ratelimit-reset: 60
ratelimit-policy: 120;w=60
```

The values track your account's own `requests_per_minute`, so a key with a
lower override reports that lower number here.

Unlike the concurrency refusal below, this header block is **derived from the
gateway source** (`http.ts` `setRateLimitHeaders`, fed by `admission.ts`
`rpmAdvice`) rather than captured from a live response. Two attempts to provoke
it on 2026-09-17 could not — the concurrency bound refused the surplus requests
first, as described above. Trust the header on the response you receive over
this example.

### `concurrency_limit_exceeded`

This one is easy to reproduce: fire more requests at once than the bound
allows. Twelve concurrent `POST /v1/chat/completions` against one account on
2026-09-17 (gateway `0.3.66`) returned **4 × `200` and 8 × `429`**, which is
the concurrency limit of 4 doing exactly what it says.

The `429` below is a verbatim capture from that run, request id
`32c59a29-5fff-4cf7-8730-f982829c6594`:

```text
ratelimit-limit: 4
ratelimit-remaining: 0
ratelimit-reset: 120
retry-after: 120
```

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "The tenant concurrency limit is exhausted.",
    "type": "rate_limit_error",
    "code": "concurrency_limit_exceeded",
    "param": null,
    "request_id": "32c59a29-5fff-4cf7-8730-f982829c6594",
    "diagnostic_code": "ai_gateway.concurrency_limit_exceeded",
    "failure_cause": "concurrency_limit_exceeded",
    "failure_domain": "varity_projection",
    "lifecycle_stage": "admission",
    "action": "Retry after an active inference request finishes.",
    "retryable": true
  }
}
```

No `ratelimit-policy` was returned, as described above. The message is the
account-scoped variant, so this account was held to its own bound rather than
to a key override.

**`120` is not the limit, and it is not a constant.** It is the retry value
*that one response* carried, because the nearest in-flight request at that
instant was contracted to settle 120 seconds out. Another refusal seconds later
will carry a different number, and a shorter-deadline workload will carry a much
smaller one. Read the header every time; never hardcode what you saw once.

`Retry-After` and `RateLimit-Reset` name the same instant, and it is not a
guess: every in-flight request carries the deadline it is contracted to settle
by, the serving replica aborts at that deadline, and the refusal reports the
**nearest** of them — the soonest moment a slot can free. Treat it as an upper
bound on the wait: a slot usually frees earlier, when a request simply
finishes.

`RateLimit-Policy` is deliberately **absent** on a concurrency refusal, and it
is the only pacing header that is. The header's `w` parameter is mandatory and
names the window the limit is counted over — but a concurrency bound is not
counted over a window at all. Four in flight is not four per anything. Emitting
`4;w=37` would assert a throughput policy that does not exist, and a client
would then pace itself by it. The per-minute refusal, which *is* windowed,
carries `ratelimit-policy: 120;w=60`.

If no in-flight deadline could be read, `Retry-After` and `RateLimit-Reset` are
both omitted rather than guessed. Fall back to your own backoff when they are
not present.

### `upstream_rate_limited`

A `429` can also come from the model provider rather than from your Varity
budget. Its code is `upstream_rate_limited`, its `failure_domain` is
`supplier_observed`, and it is retryable. It carries `Retry-After` **only when
the provider published its own reset**; when the provider did not, no
`Retry-After` is sent. Branch on `error.code`, not on the status, to tell a
Varity budget refusal from provider backpressure.

## Inference Reads: 120 Per 60 Seconds

`GET /v1/inference/policy`, `/v1/inference/requests`, `/v1/inference/usage`, and
`/v1/inference/performance` share one budget of 120 requests per 60-second
window, keyed to the authenticated account.

These four routes emit standard headers on **every** response that passes the
limiter, not only on a refusal:

| Header | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `RateLimit-Policy` | `120;w=60` — the budget and its window. |
| `RateLimit-Limit` | Requests allowed in the current window. |
| `RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in the current window. |
| `RateLimit-Reset` | Seconds until the window resets. |
| `Retry-After` | On the `429` only. |

Legacy `X-RateLimit-*` headers are not emitted here. Do not depend on them.

A refusal is `429` with `code: "rate_limit_exceeded"` and the message
`Too many managed inference requests.`

The budget is applied **after** authentication, so a `401` never carries
`RateLimit-*` headers. You will only see them on a request that authenticated
successfully.

## Public Discovery Is Not Rate Limited

`GET /v1/models` and `GET /v1/openapi.json` take no credential and the gateway
applies no request budget to them. They return **no** `RateLimit-*` headers, so
there is nothing to program against there:

```bash
curl -sSI https://ai.varity.app/v1/models
```

```text
HTTP/2 200
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
vary: accept-encoding
x-request-id: …
```

Poll the catalog as often as you need; it is served from the gateway's own
state, not from a provider.

## Account Routes

The key, billing, and policy-change routes on this host take a Developer Portal
session token, not an inference API key. Their budgets are separate again:

| Routes | Budget | Window |
|--------|--------|--------|
| `GET /v1/keys`, `GET /v1/keys/audit` | 300 requests | 1 minute |
| `POST /v1/keys` (mint a key) | 30 requests | 1 hour |
| `POST /v1/keys/{id}/revoke` | 120 requests | 1 minute |
| `/v1/billing/balance`, `/transactions`, `/settings`, `/top-up` | 120 requests | 1 minute |
| `PUT /v1/inference/policy` | Shares the 120-per-minute [inference-reads](#inference-reads-120-per-60-seconds) budget | 1 minute |

Revocation gets its own generous per-minute budget on purpose: a leaked key you
cannot revoke stays live, so a safety control is never throttled into
unavailability by the hourly creation budget.

## Size Ceilings Are Not Request Budgets

These are enforced by the request contract, not by a budget, and they return
`413` or `415` rather than `429`.

| Route | Body ceiling | Per-part ceiling |
|-------|--------------|------------------|
| `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/embeddings` | 2 MB JSON | — |
| `/v1/images/generations`, `/v1/images/edits` | 68 MB JSON | Source image or mask must be under 25 MB decoded |
| `/v1/audio/transcriptions` | ~34 MB JSON | Audio must be under 25 MB decoded |
| `/v1/audio/speech` | 1 MB JSON | — |

The image and audio body ceilings are derived from the per-part ceiling rather
than picked independently: base64 inflates by 4/3, and an image-edit request may
carry both a source image and a mask.

- A body over the ceiling returns `413` with `code: "invalid_request"`.
- A body that is not valid JSON returns `400` with `code: "invalid_request"`.
- `multipart/form-data` on `/v1/images/edits` or `/v1/audio/transcriptions`
  returns `415` with `code: "invalid_request"`. These two routes take JSON with
  base64 parts; see [Compatibility](/ai-gateway/compatibility/#the-two-sdk-exceptions).

## Retrying Correctly

```python
import time, random, requests

def call(url, **kw):
    for attempt in range(6):
        r = requests.post(url, **kw)
        if r.status_code != 429:
            return r

        # Every 429 states its own wait when it knows one: a window for the
        # per-minute bound, the nearest in-flight deadline for the concurrency
        # bound, the provider's reset for upstream_rate_limited. Fall back to
        # local backoff only when the header is absent.
        wait = float(r.headers.get("Retry-After", 2 ** attempt))
        time.sleep(wait + random.uniform(0, 1))  # jitter

    raise RuntimeError("rate limit not cleared")
```

Three rules that matter in practice:

1. **Add jitter.** A fleet that all reads `Retry-After: 60` and wakes together
   re-exhausts the budget instantly.
2. **Bound your own concurrency.** The default is 4 in flight for the whole
   account. A worker pool wider than that will spend most of its requests
   collecting `concurrency_limit_exceeded`.
3. **Branch on `error.code`, never on `message`.** Messages are written for
   people and can be reworded; `code`, `retryable`, and the HTTP status are the
   contract.

- **[Compatibility](/ai-gateway/compatibility/)**: the supported surface and every error code
- **[Rate Limits](/api/limits/)**: the separate budgets for the `varity.app/api` platform API

## AI Gateway Models

URL: https://docs.varity.so/ai-gateway/models/
Description: Ids, makers, modalities, context windows, completion limits, tool-calling and streaming support, and per-unit pricing in the live Varity AI Gateway model catalog.

The catalog is served live. This page is a snapshot of it; the endpoint is the
source of truth:

```bash
curl https://ai.varity.app/v1/models
```

`GET /v1/models` is public and needs no API key. It returns an OpenAI-shaped
`{ "object": "list", "data": [...] }` response plus a top-level
`privacy_scope`, the privacy floor the public catalog is projected at
(`"anonymized"` on this unauthenticated route). Varity adds fields OpenAI does
not return on each entry: `display_name`, `maker`, `capabilities`,
`context_window`, `max_completion_tokens`, `privacy`, `privacy_routes`,
`availability`, `refreshed_at`, and `customer_pricing`.

Do not hardcode the catalog. Resolve models at runtime from `/v1/models` and read
`capabilities` per model. The catalog changes without a docs release.

## Catalog

The catalog is not chat-only. Each entry's `capabilities.output_modalities`
says what the model produces: `text` (chat completions), `embedding`, `image`,
or `audio` (speech). Transcription models take `audio` in and return `text`.
Read `availability.status` per model from the endpoint rather than from this
page. See
[Availability is withheld, not assumed](#availability-is-withheld-not-assumed)
for what the other statuses mean.

Pass an entry's `id` verbatim as the `model` field of a request on the matching
route. Ids are readable human slugs, for example `glm-5-2`, `llama-3-3-70b`, and
`gpt-4o`. `display_name` is a separate human label, not an identifier.

`maker` says who built the model, never who serves it (`owned_by` is always
`varity`). It carries a stable slug `key` and a human `label`; the key is
`unreported`, with the label `Maker not published`, when no maker evidence was
observed.

Prices are USD, taken from each model's `customer_pricing` object, and the
`unit` differs by modality: see [Pricing](#pricing) below.

This page carries no model table on purpose. A snapshot of ids, context windows,
capabilities, and prices is stale the moment the catalog changes, so query
`GET /v1/models` and read the fields below instead.

## Reading The Catalog Fields

Each entry in `data` carries these Varity fields:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| `id` | string | Pass this as `model` in a request |
| `display_name` | string | Human label only, never an identifier |
| `maker.key` | string | Stable slug of who built the model, for example `zai`; `unreported` when unknown |
| `maker.label` | string | Human maker label, for example `Z.ai` |
| `capabilities.input_modalities` | array | What a request may carry: `text`, `image`, `document`, `audio`, `video`. A model without `document` rejects a `document` content part with `400 input_modality_unsupported` |
| `capabilities.output_modalities` | array | What the model produces: `text`, `embedding`, `image`, `audio` |
| `capabilities.chat_completions` | boolean | `true` on the chat models only; image, audio, and embedding models report `false`. Read it per model |
| `capabilities.tool_calls` | boolean | Supported on a subset of the catalog; read it per model |
| `capabilities.streaming` | boolean | Supported on most, not all, chat models; read it per model |
| `capabilities.streaming_tool_calls` | boolean | Narrower than `streaming`; read it per model. Absent on a few entries, which means unproven, not unsupported |
| `capabilities.transcription` | boolean | `true` when `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` accepts the model |
| `capabilities.speech` | boolean | `true` when `POST /v1/audio/speech` accepts the model; `speech_formats` lists its output formats |
| `context_window` | integer | Total tokens, input plus output |
| `max_completion_tokens` | integer | Ceiling on generated tokens |
| `privacy` | string | Routing privacy class. The live catalog contains both `"private"` and `"anonymized"` entries |
| `privacy_routes` | array | Route set matching `privacy` |
| `availability.status` | string | `"available"`, `"last_known_available"`, `"temporarily_unavailable"`, `"verification_stale"`, or `"unverified"`, with an `observed_at` timestamp and, on the last three, a `reason` |
| `customer_pricing` | object | See below |
| `refreshed_at` | string | When the gateway last refreshed the entry |

### Availability Is Withheld, Not Assumed

A model stays listed in `/v1/models` when its routes are unhealthy — it is not
removed — but it stops claiming to be callable. The gateway publishes a route
as available only once that route has **succeeded** since its last failure. A
route whose provider refused Varity's credential, or that failed for any other
reason, is excluded from the published projection until a real success clears
it; a routing layer's periodic retry of a failing route is a trial request, not
evidence of health, and is deliberately not borrowed by the catalog.

When a model has no publishable route left, its entry changes rather than
disappearing:

| `availability.status` | `reason` | Meaning |
|-----------------------|----------|---------|
| `available` | — | A route succeeded recently. Callable. |
| `last_known_available` | — | The entry is being served from the last good observation; `observed_at` is when that was. |
| `temporarily_unavailable` | `route_temporarily_unavailable` | Routes exist but none is currently publishable. Expect `503 model_unavailable` if you call it. |
| `verification_stale` | `route_verification_stale` | The route's capability certification is too old to stand behind. |
| `unverified` | `route_unverified` | The route was never certified for this capability. |

The affected `capabilities` flags go `false` alongside the status, so a model
that cannot currently serve chat reports `chat_completions: false` rather than
advertising a capability the next request would be refused for.

This health state is held per gateway replica, in process, and is not shared
between them. A replica that has observed a route failing will withhold it
while a replica that has not yet seen one may still publish it, so two reads of
`/v1/models` seconds apart can legitimately disagree during a provider
incident. Treat `availability` as a strong hint, not a guarantee, and always
handle `503 model_unavailable` at call time.

### Pricing

Every model in the current catalog returns `customer_pricing.status: "configured"`
with concrete numbers. The schema also allows `status: "not_configured"`, which
carries no other fields, so branch on `status` before reading a rate:

```json
"customer_pricing": {
  "status": "configured",
  "version": "2026-07-28.v3.d74e3f5155b10314",
  "observed_at": "2026-08-01T02:30:58.677Z",
  "currency": "usd",
  "unit": "per_million_tokens",
  "input": "<number>",
  "output": "<number>",
  "cached_input": "<number>"
}
```

The rates are placeholders here; they are numbers in the live response.

`currency` is always `usd`. `unit` takes one of four values, and it decides
which fields carry the rate:

| `unit` | Models | Where the rate is |
|--------|--------|-------------------|
| `per_million_tokens` | Chat and embedding models | `input` and `output` per million tokens; `cached_input` for cached prompt tokens |
| `per_image` | Image generation and editing models | `request`, a flat price per generated image; `input`, `output`, and `cached_input` are `0` |
| `per_million_characters` | Speech models | `input` per million characters of text; `output` and `cached_input` are `0` |
| `per_audio_second` | Transcription models | `input` per second of audio; `output` and `cached_input` are `0` |

`request` is present only on `per_image` entries. `cached_input` is per model:
some models price cached input tokens below `input`, others at the same rate.
Always read `unit` and `currency` rather than
assuming; the `version` string identifies the immutable price set the numbers
came from and `observed_at` says when the gateway last observed it. Rates are
the current managed rate for the model's preferred route, not a permanent
guarantee: each admitted request snapshots its own price before it runs.

Input and output prices both vary widely across the catalog and change with it,
so read `customer_pricing` per model instead of carrying a range from this page.

### Context Windows

Context windows vary per model, and `max_completion_tokens` is a separate, much
smaller ceiling on any single response. A large context window does not imply a
large answer, so read both fields per model.

## Picking A Model

- **Need tool calling?** Only a subset of the catalog accepts `tools` / `tool_choice`, and fewer support them while streaming. Read `capabilities.tool_calls` and `capabilities.streaming_tool_calls` per model, and see [Compatibility](/ai-gateway/compatibility/).
- **Need a very large context?** Sort the live catalog by `context_window`. The Grok 4.20 entries (`grok-4-20`, `grok-4-20-multi-agent`) have the widest windows in the current catalog, but read the field rather than assuming.
- **Cost sensitive?** Compare `customer_pricing.input` across the live catalog, within one `unit`. Embedding models carry the lowest token rates; among chat models, `mercury-2-5` and `glm-4-7-flash` have the lowest input rates in the current catalog.

There is no per-model retrieval route. `GET /v1/models/{id}` returns `404`; fetch
the list and filter it client-side.

- **[AI Gateway Overview](/ai-gateway/)**: base URL, auth, and the quickstart snippets
- **[Compatibility](/ai-gateway/compatibility/)**: supported and unsupported OpenAI surface

## AI Gateway Playground

URL: https://docs.varity.so/ai-gateway/playground/
Description: Try AI Gateway models in the Developer Portal, compare them, search the web, attach files, and let the assistant work on your connected repository and deployments.

The Playground is the first tab of the AI Gateway page in the Developer
Portal. It sends real requests through the AI Gateway, so they
are charged to your gateway balance and count against the same account rate
limits as your API keys.

## Choosing A Model

Pick any model from the live catalog. A tool the selected model cannot use is
shown as unavailable, and its tooltip says why.

## The "+" Menu

**Add**

- **Files** and **Folder**: attach files, or a whole folder, to your message.
- **Create image**: choose an image model and open its workspace.

**Tools**

- **Web search**: search the web and cite sources.
- **Read links**: read the pages linked in your message.
- **Deep research**: several private web searches, then one cited answer.
- **Compare models**: send one prompt to 2 or 3 models side by side.
- **Varity tools**: let the assistant work with your deployments, repository,
  and builds (see below).

**Connect**

- **Repository**: choose the GitHub repository the assistant works on.
- **Connectors**: add remote MCP servers. A connector tool that is not marked
  read-only asks you to **Run** or **Don't run** before it executes.

## Varity Tools

With Varity tools on, the assistant can:

- list your deployments and read their status and logs;
- list, search, and read files in the connected repository;
- search and read these docs;
- get a price quote and plan a new deployment;
- plan a redeploy, an environment change, or a deletion;
- propose a code change as a pull request, read a pull request and its CI status,
  and plan its merge;
- plan deploying a commit.

Anything that changes your account is a plan first. You approve each step, such
as the commit and then the deploy, before it runs.

Varity tools are available only on models that support streamed tool calls, and
they add input tokens to every message. The menu shows the approximate cost.

## Workspace Panel

Open the side panel for:

- **Files**: open a file from the chat or the connected repository.
- **Browser**: open a deployed app, or any https address.
- **Terminal**: follow a deployment's runtime logs. It is read-only and runs no
  commands.

## View Code

**View code** shows the exact request the Playground would send for the current
message, so you can copy it into your own app.

## History, Projects, Memory, And Incognito

- **History and projects**: conversations are grouped into projects and kept on
  your device, not on Varity's servers. The AI Gateway stores no prompt or
  response content.
- **Memory**: notes you save on your device. While memory is on, they are sent
  with each message, and you can see them in View code.
- **Incognito**: an incognito chat is not saved to history and does not use
  memory. It ends when you leave it.

The Playground uses the same privacy floor as your account. See
[Privacy Routing](/ai-gateway/compatibility/#privacy-routing).

## Next Steps

- **[AI Gateway Overview](/ai-gateway/)**: call the same models from your code
- **[Billing and Keys](/ai-gateway/billing-and-keys/)**: credits and inference keys
